title: Add ShellPlay quickstart and lightweight RAG runtime docs
author: Priya Nair
description:
This PR adds a compact ShellPlay quickstart and companion lightweight RAG runtime documentation targeted at developers who want a minimal local authoring loop for retrieval-augmented generation. Motivation: many users ask for a tiny, reproducible authoring surface that demonstrates end-to-end RAG (index -> query -> tool-call -> structured output) without requiring a full orchestration stack. ShellPlay is a single-folder quickstart that uses the local RAG runtime shim (lightweight, no GPU required) and a devcontainer for a predictable onboarding experience.

What this change includes: checklist and high-level notes: 
- New quickstart guide: docs/quickstarts/shellplay/README.md (tutorial, goals, and tips). 
- Step-by-step devcontainer: .devcontainer/devcontainer.json + Dockerfile (prebuilt indexer and a small SQLite-backed index). 
- Example playbook and tool stubs: examples/shellplay/playbook.yaml, examples/shellplay/tools/email_stub.py, examples/shellplay/tools/search_stub.py. 
- Structured output validation section: docs/quickstarts/shellplay/structured-output.md with JSON Schema snippets and a compact linter command. 
- Local telemetry probes: docs/quickstarts/shellplay/telemetry.md and a minimal probes config (telemetry/probes.yaml) so engineers can see token breakdowns and latency traces in the console. 
- Migration / compatibility notes: compatibility with Hosted API and Redwood Private (mapping table + quick migration commands). 
- Tests: quickstart smoke test (ci/quickstarts/shellplay-smoke.yml) that runs the devcontainer, creates index, and validates two example queries.

Design decisions and guidance: 
- Keep the quickstart small: the runtime shim intentionally omits batching and advanced KV-cache features; it is designed for authoring and functional tests, not production. The docs call this out and provide a link to production-focused pages. 
- Structured-output-first: the quickstart emphasizes defining and validating output contracts early. We show how to run the lightweight linter locally and how to add contract-based regression tests to Redwood Optimize. 
- Security caveat: example tool stubs run locally and are clearly labeled as insecure by default; production integration guidance includes KMS/HSM notes and audit logging references. 

Checklist completed before merge: 
- [x] Tutorial walkthrough written and validated in devcontainer. 
- [x] Example tool stubs and playbook tested locally. 
- [x] CI quickstart smoke job added and green. 
- [x] Telemetry probe example included and documented. 
- [x] Docs cross-links to existing RAG authoring pages and SDK snippets.

Related: this PR is companion to redwood-examples#338412 (sandboxed plugin hotreload) and to an internal ENG task to unify quickstart devcontainers (ENG-4729).
